findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is on the side opposite to the idea. The mean unusual move in the short direction is -0.87 % per case over 5 days (t -0.70, cases of one day taken together, 67 days, 80 cases), which is -0.045 of the coin's usual 10.60 % move. The overshoot slope is also negative (-0.009), so larger breaks gave back no more than small ones.
findings.F2: I recomputed choppy-market closes above the prior 20-day high on folds B and C, keeping the first case per 5-day cell (30 cases, plain t per case). Over every horizon from 3 days on, the move after the break continues upward rather than fading: the fade is -1.46 % over 3 days (t -0.94), -3.83 % over 5 days (t -1.58) and -4.66 % over 10 days (t -1.34). Only the 1-day move leans the idea's way, at +0.48 % (t 0.45).
findings.F3: The give-back is not graded by the overshoot. Over 5 days, the choppy upside breaks fade by -1.78 % for the smallest third of overshoots (t -0.51), -6.90 % for the middle third (t -1.29) and -2.55 % for the largest third (t -0.76), with 10 cases each.
findings.F4: The fade does not live in one coin or period; it is scattered across small groups. Over 5 days, only XMR fades clearly (+5.21 %, t 2.93, 7 cases) and LTC barely (+0.52 %, 5 cases). BTC, ETH, XRP and ZEC continue (-9.91 %, -12.30 %, -10.89 % and -2.50 %). 2018 and 2019 fade (+4.60 %, 6 cases; +2.22 %, 3 cases), while 2020 and 2021 continue (-2.61 %, 8 cases; -9.68 %, t -2.28, 13 cases).
findings.F5: The choppy profile does not separate failed breaks from real ones, as the brief requires. Upside breaks continue in a rising market (5-day fade -4.77 %, t -2.96, 103 cases) about as much as in a choppy one (-3.83 %). Choppy downside breaks (11 cases) fade only over 1 to 3 days (+3.06 %, t 1.05; +3.01 %, t 1.62) and then continue (5 days -7.00 %, t -1.47; 10 days -12.91 %, t -2.40).
findings.F6: Cost is not what decided this test. The total move per case is -1.45 %, which is 7.5 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade but on the losing side, so no holding period or sizing turns this short into a paying book.

no_ideas: In choppy markets, closes beyond the 20-day range do not fade in these data. They continue at every horizon from 3 days on, with no grading by overshoot and no difference from trending markets, and the few fading groups are scattered and small (F2–F5), so the theme's effect is not in the data.
